newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge sees end of AXA study by May.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge sees end of AXA study by May.

text.p: Belgian insurer Royale Belge said on Thursday it will probably say in May to what extent it will link with domestic rival AXA Belgium following the merger of the two companies' French parents, respectively UAP and AXA, to form AXA-UAP.

"Different working groups have been set up to look at what might happen. It will take several weeks, and certainly not before the end of March, before decisions are taken," Royale Belge Chief Executive Officer Jean-Pierre Gerard told a news conference on 1996 results.
"I hope that for the annual general meeting on May 28 we will have the results of these studies and they can be announced," Gerard added.
Gerard declined to speculate on whether it was feasible to fully merge with AXA Belgium or combine the companies' Dutch businesses.
AXA Belgium's chief executive said last week closer association was natural, but presented various difficulties, as it could damage relationship with brokers and agents.
Gerard announced that AXA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Claude Bebear had now joined Royale Belge's board, following its link with UAP. He replaces Didier Pfeiffer.
Recent AXA-UAP recruit Denis Kessler, formerly head of the French insurance industry federation, had also joined Royale Belge's board, replacing Jacques-Henri Gougenheim.
The changes took effect on Thursday.
